text:
Predicates:
ProvidesFinancialAid(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
ProveHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
LivesInFamily(x) ::: x lives in a family.
HasBeenUnemployed(x) ::: x's parent has been out of work.
Applying(x, y) ::: x is applying to y.
Cost(y, z) ::: the cost of y is z.
CheaperThan(y, z) ::: y is cheaper than z.
GRE(y) ::: y is the GRE test.
ETS ::: the organization providing aid.

Premises:
Cost(GRE, 205) ∧ CheaperThan(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (ProveHardship(x) → (SingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x))) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources can prove hardship.
LiveInFamily(Tom) ∧ SingleParentFamily(Tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
HasBeenUnemployed(Tom'sFather) ::: Tom's dad has been out of work.
FewResources(Tom) ::: Tom has few resources.
Applying(Tom, GRE) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.

Conclusion:
ProvidesFinancialAid(ETS, Tom) ::: ETS provides financial aid to Tom.
